text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - The London stock market ended on a resilient note, clawing back most of the losses triggered mid-afternoon by a smaller-than-expected rise in U.S. jobless claims which hit U.S. equities and debt prices. The FTSE 100 share index had dropped as low as 3,981.2 points in the afternoon as U.S. shares sagged in early trade. But bid speculation, gains among insurers and Wall Street's subsequent rebound dragged the FTSE back up to end at 3,994.7, down 14.6 points.

FRANKFURT- German stocks extend losses to close floor-trade lower amid Wall Street worries and a weaker German debt market. The 30-share DAX closed down 22.24 points to 2,680.75. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 2,683.52.

PARIS - French shares closed sharply lower, in line with an opening fall on Wall Street after a surprise decline in U.S. unemployment claims, investors are now focusing on Friday's U.S. retail sales and producer price data for interest rate prospects. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 11.08 points or 0.52 percent to 2,135.63.

ZURICH - A feeble early Wall Street put Swiss shares under pressure in late trade and the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) fell below the important level of 3,800 points, shares of watchmaker SMH fell 2.9 percent or 25 Swiss francs to 822 francs on a negative study of the Smart Car joint venture with Mercedes. The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was down 0.2 percent or 4.85 points to 2,430.54.

TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market is closed on Thursday for a national holiday and will reopen on Friday. On Wednesday, the key 225-share Nikkei average lost 167.70 points or 0.80 percent to finish at 20,870.83.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong shares ended down slightly, just shy of Wednesday's record closing high, due to profit-taking on some of the market's better performers. The Hang Seng index eased 8.10 points to close at 12,242.47.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market finished on a firmer note with blue chips reversing early falls after a weaker-than-expected September jobs report spurred renewed speculation of a near-term interest rate cut. The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed 12.8 points higher at 2,323.5.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares closed near their day lows as a weaker Wall Street led global markets away from their recent record highs. Wall Street stocks, after dipping on Wednesday, opened weaker after new jobless claims data triggered renewed concern about tightness in the U.S. labour market. The All-share index fell 27.6 points to 7,031.5, as Industrials dipped 28.7 points to 8,238.7 and the Gold index ended down 2.8 points to 1,740.0.
